Wrong belief "squares the gate count" gives 16, not 8.
Wrong belief "adds two wires regardless of gate count" gives 6, not 8.

questions.explanation: Each of the 4 gates needs two input wires and no wires are shared, so the circuit requires 8 external inputs.
questions.hint: Two input wires per gate, all distinct.

questions.learningObjective: Solve problems involving logic circuits and truth tables.
questions.stem: Under this scenario, a combinational circuit has 9 two-valued inputs and one output. Altogether how many rows are in its truth chart?
questions.explanation: With 9 binary inputs there are 2 to the power 9 distinct input combinations, so the truth table has 512 rows. The required result is 512.
questions.hint: Each input doubles the number of rows.
